transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. I'm here because when I'm alone working late, I start eating and it feels like I can't stop or control how much I'm eating until it's over. It's really starting to worry me and I feel like I need some help.
During these episodes of eating, do you feel a sense of guilt, shame, or self-criticism afterwards?

Yes, I feel an intense amount of shame and self-criticism afterward, and the next day I feel so sluggish and embarrassed that I just want to hide in my apartment. I’ve even started waiting until my roommate goes to bed to eat in secret because I'm so terrified of her seeing the food and judging me.
How often do these episodes of uncontrolled eating happen, and do you ever try to compensate for them by purging, using laxatives, or excessively exercising afterwards?

These episodes have been happening at least once a week for about ten months, sometimes more when my work deadlines pile up. I don't purge, use laxatives, or exercise excessively to compensate; instead, I just feel incredibly sluggish and ashamed, and I end up shutting myself in my apartment the next day.
Can you describe a typical episode of uncontrolled eating, including what types of food you usually eat and whether you eat more rapidly than normal during these episodes?

Yes, I eat incredibly fast, barely chewing and just swallowing until everything is suddenly gone and I can't even remember what it tasted like. During a typical episode, I'll order enough takeout for three people—like two entrees, extra sides, and dessert—and then still polish off half a family-size bag of chips and whatever is in my freezer within an hour or two while I'm working.
During these episodes, do you typically eat until you're uncomfortably full, or is it more about eating rapidly and being unable to stop, regardless of feeling full?

It is actually a combination of both; I eat incredibly fast, barely chewing or tasting the food while feeling completely unable to stop or control my hands. I don't actually stop until my stomach feels painfully tight, bloated, and uncomfortable to the point where I have to lean back because it hurts to sit up straight.
During these episodes of rapid and uncontrolled eating, do you usually eat alone due to embarrassment or because you're genuinely unaware of the amount of food you're consuming until it's over?

I definitely eat alone because of the intense embarrassment and shame. I wait until my roommate goes to sleep and the lights are off, then sneak the food into my room to eat on the floor so she won't see the pile of containers and judge me. While I do feel a bit detached and eat incredibly fast, the primary reason I hide away is because I'm just so ashamed of how much I'm consuming.
Can you tell me if you have ever had periods where you didn't experience these episodes of uncontrolled eating for several months at a time, or have they been fairly consistent over the past year?

No, they have been very consistent over the past ten months without any breaks at all. Ever since I took on my senior designer role, I've had these episodes at least once a week, and even more often when my work deadlines pile up.
Have you ever experienced any significant weight fluctuations or concerns about your weight that led to restrictive eating patterns or fears of gaining weight?

No, I haven't really experienced significant weight fluctuations or engaged in restrictive eating due to fears of gaining weight. My main concern has really just been the out-of-control eating episodes themselves and how much they are affecting my life.
Can you estimate how many times a month you have these episodes of uncontrolled eating, and are they typically triggered by emotional states, such as stress or anxiety, rather than hunger?

I have these episodes at least four times a month, and even more often when my work deadlines pile up. They are definitely triggered by work stress and pressure rather than physical hunger. In fact, I often start eating late at night even when I'm already full and my body is giving me zero hunger signals.

Can you confirm if you have experienced these episodes of uncontrolled eating, on average, at least once a week for the past three months, which is a key factor in differentiating between my current considerations for your diagnosis?

Yes, I can absolutely confirm that. It has been happening at least once a week, and sometimes even more when my work stress peaks, for the past ten months straight. So it has definitely been a consistent issue for the last three months as well.
